newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to import 1.8 mln tonnes crude in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to import 1.8 mln tonnes crude in 1997.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) plans to import up to 1.8 million tonnes of crude oil this year under five term contracts, a CPC official said on Tuesday.
"We have budgeted for 1.8 million tonnes this year, slightly less than the almost two million tonnes of crude imported in 1996 because of the refinery shut down," he told Reuters.
The CPC shut down its 50,000-60,000 barrels-per-day oil refinery on January 15 for five weeks for routine maintenance, prompting more imports of refined oil products such as diesel and jet fuel.
The last maintenance shutdown of Sri Lanka's only refinery at Sapugaskanda, just north of Colombo, was in January-February 1995.
CPC officials said almost half the crude imports will be from Iran. It plans to buy 780,000 tonnes of Iranian light crude from the National Iranian Oil Company.
The CPC will also buy 330,000 tonnes of Arabian light crude from the Saudi Arabian Oil Company and 300,000 tonnes of very light Miri crude from Petronas Malaysia, they said.
The CPC will also import 180,000 tonnes of Upper Zakum crude from the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company and 120,000 tonnes of Gulf of Suez mixed crude from Egypt, CPC officials said.
The balance crude imports will be decided later on, they said.
Sri Lanka usually buys light crude which the refinery is designed to process because of the island's need for diesel and kerosene.
